skills.name: Care and maintenance of tools and appliances

note.text:
Maintenance is keeping tools and appliances in good working condition so that they last longer and are safe.
• Preventive maintenance: regular care before a breakdown: cleaning, oiling moving parts, tightening screws, checking cables, keeping devices dry and covered.
• Corrective maintenance: repairing after a breakdown: replacing a fuse, a bulb or a worn part.
Good habits: read the user manual; switch off and unplug before cleaning; use the right voltage; do not overload sockets; store tools clean and dry; oil metal tools against rust; replace damaged cables at once.
A fuse is a thin wire that melts if too much current flows, cutting the circuit and protecting the appliance.

worked_example.problem: An iron stops working. The technician finds that the fuse in the plug has melted. What should be done, and why did it happen?
steps: The fuse melted because too much current flowed (a fault or overload).
Find and repair the fault, then replace the fuse with one of the correct rating.
worked_example.answer: Find the fault and replace the fuse with the correct rating.

cards.idea: Preventive maintenance is regular care before a breakdown.
Corrective maintenance is repairing after a breakdown.
Always switch off and unplug before cleaning an appliance.

pick.q: Why should metal tools be oiled before storing them?
w: to make them slippery to hold
pick.y: Oil keeps out air and water.

pick.q: Why should you not plug many appliances into one socket?
pick.r: It overloads the socket and can cause a fire.
w: It is required by the manual.
pick.y: Too much current heats the wires.

pick.s: Oiling a sewing machine every month.
Dusting a computer and its fan.
Changing a broken cable of a radio.

questions.prompt: Is this preventive or corrective maintenance? {X.s}

misconceptions.explain: Ask: is the work done before or after a breakdown?

solution: Preventive: before a breakdown; corrective: after a breakdown.
